transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-21
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen, Priya Kapoor, Liam O'Neill (Redwood) / Michael Park, Sara Lopez, Jamal Reed, Nina Gomez (BlueWave)

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:05] Michael Park: Yep we can hear you, thanks Alex.
[00:10] Alex Chen: Cool. Quick agenda — align on success criteria, run through workload numbers, pick bench tests and timelines, and then map those to hosted vs dedicated vs private trade offs. Priya from our SE team will cover perf/bench details.
[00:28] Priya Kapoor: Hi all, I'll go over the benchmark plan. Quick note — transcriber might show Redwood "Dedicate" sometimes, so ignore typos.
[00:35] Sara Lopez: ha yeah we've seen that in other calls too.
[00:40] Priya Kapoor: For the POC we typically measure: p50/p90/p99 latency, tokens-per-second throughput at several concurrency points, end-to-end tail latency including network, and quality/regression on a red team of prompts. We'll also capture cost estimates per 1M tokens.
[01:12] Jamal Reed: For our app the important bits: peak QPS is around 45 requests/sec, average sequence length ~220 tokens, 1-2k concurrent users but concurrency for inference is about 60-80 concurrent requests. We care a lot about p99 < 400ms for short prompts.
[01:40] Priya Kapoor: Got it. That workload sits in a spot where batching helps a lot but we have to control latency. For hosted — we can hit your p99 at reasonable cost with our optimized kernels and caching for common prefixes. Dedicated gives you more predictable throughput and isolation; Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you full control for data residency and KMS integration but needs more lead time.
[02:10] Nina Gomez: Security is non-negotiable. We need SOC2 docs, SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and we'd prefer KMS-managed keys. Also data residency for EU objects might matter down the road.
[02:30] Alex Chen: We'll share SOC2/ISO artifacts and our private deployment checklist — action item. For KMS, both Dedicated and Private support customer-managed keys, hosted can integrate with KMS in certain regions — we'll clarify.
[02:50] Michael Park: Timeline question: how fast can you stand up a dedicated pool vs hosted access? We want to run benches in two weeks if possible.
[03:05] Liam O'Neill: Hosted access is immediate — you can start benching within hours. Dedicated typically takes 2–4 weeks for reserved capacity provisioning depending on region and commit. Private (VPC or on-prem) is usually 4–8 weeks including network setup and security review.
[03:30] Speaker 2: (background) sorry can you say the dedication timeline again?
[03:34] Liam O'Neill: Yeah dedicated 2-4 weeks.
[03:36] Sara Lopez: For us the decision will be: if hosted meets latency+cost, we'd prefer that since less ops overhead. If not, we want dedicated. Private is a last step for strict compliance.
[03:52] Priya Kapoor: That's a common pattern. For the POC we'll run a three-phase bench: 1) smoke & baseline on hosted (single model variant) to validate p50/p99, 2) scaled runs to reproduce peak QPS and measure batching efficiency, 3) a dedicated pilot (if needed) to validate reserved capacity and network topology. We'll also run a small private deploy checklist in parallel to validate config and KMS if you want.
[04:30] Jamal Reed: For bench specifics — we'd like tests that mimic our typical multi-turn chat flows, include context sizes up to 2k tokens, and include a rerank workload (short prompts but high QPS).
[04:48] Priya Kapoor: Good call — we'll include a reranker micro-benchmark and multi-turn test with KV cache warmup. Note on transcriptions: sometimes it writes KV "cash" which is wrong.
[05:02] Alex Chen: On metrics, we'll capture: p50/p90/p99, median & tail token/sec, CPU/GPU utilization, request batching stats, and cost per 1M tokens. For quality — we'll run a small eval set and compute BLEU/ROUGE-ish scores and manual spot checks for hallucination rate.
[05:28] Michael Park: How do you handle graceful degradation — if capacity is limited do you fall back to smaller model or queue?
[05:40] Priya Kapoor: We have automated fallback policies — route to compatible model variants (smaller quantized), or burst to dedicated spare capacity if configured. There's also a queued mode but we avoid queued for user-facing low latency flows.
[05:58] Sara Lopez: We're curious about quantization — does Redwood recommend int8 for our workload? We care about quality drop.
[06:10] Priya Kapoor: We'll run quality vs cost matrix in POC. Some models are quantization-friendly with minimal quality impact; we'll include a quantization profile test.
[06:22] Michael Park: Pricing is important — can you give a ballpark for hosted vs dedicated?
[06:28] Alex Chen: Ballpark — hosted per-token is higher but no infra ops. Dedicated reduces unit cost by ~30\u201350% depending on utilization commitments. Private might be comparable to dedicated plus support/license fees. We'll send a preliminary pricing sheet.
[06:45] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[06:48] Jamal Reed: For success criteria — we propose: 1) p99 < 400ms on typical prompts, 2) end-to-end cost per 1M tokens under $X (we'll share target), 3) no regression in quality beyond 2% on our eval set, 4) SOC2/SSO compatibility validated.
[07:12] Priya Kapoor: That sounds reasonable. We'll instrument the bench to measure those exact metrics and produce a one-page scorecard.
[07:22] Alex Chen: Let's talk setup and timeline — propose 4-week POC: week 0 (this week) — planning and infra access; week 1 — hosted baseline smoke; week 2 — scaled load tests and reranker tests; week 3 — optimization & dedicated pilot if needed; week 4 — analysis, cost modeling, and exec wrap. We can accelerate parts if you want quick wins.
[07:52] Michael Park: That fits our target. Can we start the bench on 2026-07-27?
[07:57] Alex Chen: Yes. Action items assigned.
[08:00] Priya Kapoor: For benchmarks we'll need: sample payloads, concurrency targets, and a small eval set. Michael I'll follow up with a checklist.
[08:12] Sara Lopez: Network: if we go dedicated/private we need to plan VPC peering and private links; we'll loop in infra.
[08:20] Nina Gomez: Also please note we may need EU data residency for some customers; how do you support region pinning?
[08:28] Liam O'Neill: We can pin models and routes to EU regions for hosted and we can deploy Dedicated/Private in EU regions. We'll include region notes in the POC doc.
[08:40] Michael Park: Any compliance gotchas we should be aware of?
[08:44] Alex Chen: We'll share SOC2 reports and a summary of encryption at transit/rest. Private deployments allow HSM/KMS with customer key ownership.
[08:52] Priya Kapoor: For perf instrumentation we'll also capture tracing hooks so you can correlate with your app telemetry.
[08:58] Jamal Reed: Will Redwood help tune batching/kv cache settings?
[09:02] Priya Kapoor: Yes, tuning is part of the POC. We'll run automated suggestions and a few manual knobs to hit latency targets.
[09:12] Speaker 3: (brief crosstalk)
[09:18] Alex Chen: Ok to summarize: 4-week POC, starting planning now. Bench on hosted first 7/27. Redwood to send POC plan, pricing, SOC2 and private deployment checklist. BlueWave to send sample data and concurrency targets. Schedule infra meeting for VPC peering if we get to dedicated/private.
[09:42] Michael Park: That covers it for me. One more minor — competitor landscape: we'll be evaluating some bench results vs Anthropic and OpenAI to validate cost/latency tradeoffs.
[09:56] Alex Chen: Totally fair, we'll include competitor baseline notes and how we measured them.
[10:02] Sara Lopez: Thanks everyone.
[10:04] Alex Chen: Thanks — we'll follow up with docs and calendar invites.
[10:08] (call ends)

Notes: Transcript contains occasional mis-attributions and transcription errors (common in Fireflies exports). Links referenced: POC playbook deck (https://redwood.ai/decks/poc-playbook.pdf), preliminary pricing sheet (link to be shared), security docs: /sec/soc2 (will be shared by Alex).
